The '''2016–17 Scottish Premiership''' (known as the [[Ladbrokes|Ladbrokes Premiership]] for sponsorship reasons) was the fourth season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. The fixtures were published on 17 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/spfl-announces-ladbrokes-league-fixtures/ |title=The SPFL has today unveiled the fixture lists for the 2016/17 Ladbrokes Premiership, Ladbrokes Championship, Ladbrokes League 1 and Ladbrokes League 2 seasons. |website=spfl.co.uk |date=17 June 2016 |access-date=17 June 2016 |archive-date=10 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010124745/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/spfl-announces-ladbrokes-league-fixtures/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The season began on 6 August 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/start-date-for-201617-league-season/ | title=Start date for 2016/17 league season | publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] | date=25 January 2016 | access-date=25 January 2016 | archive-date=1 May 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501102614/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/start-date-for-201617-league-season/ | url-status=live }}</ref> [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] were the defending champions.

Twelve teams contested the league: [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

On 2 April 2017, Celtic won their sixth consecutive title and 48th overall after a 5–0 win away to Hearts, with eight matches still to play and would go on to complete the season [[List of unbeaten football club seasons|unbeaten]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39460870|title=Celtic win Scottish Premiership: Brendan Rodgers' side seal sixth straight title|date=2 April 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=3 April 2017|archive-date=3 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403032217/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39460870|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/apr/02/hearts-celtic-scottish-premiership-match-report|title=Five-star Celtic dispatch Hearts to secure Scottish Premiership title|date=2 April 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=3 April 2017|archive-date=16 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170416142452/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/apr/02/hearts-celtic-scottish-premiership-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/scottish-premiership/2016-2017/unbeaten-celtic-end-astonishing-season-as-invincibles-with-win-over-hearts_sto6175267/story.shtml|title=Unbeaten Celtic end astonishing season as Invincibles with win over Hearts|date=21 May 2017|access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref>

==Format==

In the initial phase of the season, each of the twelve teams play the other eleven teams three times. After 33 rounds, the league splits into two sections, a top six and a bottom six, with each team playing all the other teams in their section once. The league attempts to balance the fixture list so that teams in the same section have played each other twice at home and twice away, but sometimes this is impossible. A total of 228 matches will be played, with 38 matches played by each team.

The table lists the positions of teams after each week of matches. In order to preserve chronological progress, any postponed matches are not included in the round at which they were originally scheduled, but added to the full round they were played immediately afterwards. For example, if a match is scheduled for matchday 13, but then postponed and played between days 16 and 17, it will be added to the standings for day 16.

==Premiership play-offs==
The quarter-final was contested between the 3rd and 4th placed teams ([[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]) in the [[2016–17 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]]. After defeating Greenock Morton 5–1 over two legs, Dundee United advanced to the semi-finals to face the 2nd placed team ([[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]) in the Championship. Dundee United progressed to the play-off final following a 4–3 aggregate victory, but then lost 1–0 on aggregate to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in the final. Hamilton therefore retained their place in the Premiership for the [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership|2017–18]] season.
